extracted.intended_audience: USC researchers, faculty, staff, and students involved in research, innovation, and grant administration
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of USC Office of Research and Innovation resources, organizational responsibilities, and the institutional standards and processes that govern research, human/animal subjects oversight, research integrity, technology transfer, and internal funding/limited-submission processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: ethical and rigorous research to benefit society
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of the Office of Research and Innovation at the University of Southern California is to nurture and promote ethical and rigorous research, scholarship, creativity, and innovation to benefit society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets institutional expectations: research should be ethical, rigorous, creative, and oriented toward societal benefit; these principles underlie review, training, and administrative decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects research policies and IRB oversight (HRPP)
rubrics_metrics.description: HRPP develops program-wide policies for the conduct and review of human subjects research at USC, provides education and training, and oversees the Institutional Review Boards (IRB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All human-subjects research must follow HRPP policies, obtain IRB review/approval where required, and complete mandated education/training provided by HRPP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and use oversight (IACUC)
rubrics_metrics.description: IACUC oversees USC’s animal programs, animal facilities, and policies ensuring appropriate care, ethical use and humane treatment of animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal research must comply with IACUC policies and approvals; investigators must ensure appropriate care, ethical use, and humane treatment per committee standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research administration standards (Department of Contracts and Grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: DCG supports the research administration process, ensuring it’s consistent with university standards for academic freedom, research ethics, and fiscal responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal preparation, award acceptance, and post-award management must adhere to standards of academic freedom, research ethics, and fiscal responsibility enforced by DCG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research integrity and responsible conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: ORI fosters a culture of integrity within the entire USC research community by educating investigators about responsible conduct in research and laboratory practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators are expected to follow responsible conduct of research and laboratory practice norms; ORI provides education and programs to support compliance and culture of integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest and regulatory approvals management (RTS: diSClose and iStar)
rubrics_metrics.description: RTS maintains and supports diSClose (for managing conflicts of interest) and iStar (for research with human subjects, animals, and biohazardous and radioactive substances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers must use diSClose to disclose and manage conflicts of interest and use iStar to obtain required approvals for human-subjects, animal, biohazard, or radioactive-material research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal funding and limited-submission procedures (RII)
rubrics_metrics.description: RII supports investigators through internal funding programs, limited submissions, shared resources, as well as faculty training via the Center for Excellence in Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators seeking internal awards or participating in limited-submission opportunities must follow RII processes and use available shared resources and training; limited submissions may impose additional internal selection processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale and interdisciplinary proposal development support (RSD)
rubrics_metrics.description: RSD works with faculty and teams on developing large-scale and interdisciplinary research proposals and informing researchers about federally-funded research programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complex, large-scale, or interdisciplinary proposals, collaborate with RSD to align proposals with federal program requirements and to leverage institutional support in proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology transfer and commercialization processes (Stevens Center for Innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: USC Stevens is USC’s technology transfer office and also licenses discoveries, promotes entrepreneurship, stimulates innovation and leads corporate research collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers seeking commercialization, licensing, or corporate collaborations should engage the Stevens Center to manage intellectual property, licensing negotiations, and entrepreneurship support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biomedical commercialization support (Alfred E. Mann Institute)
rubrics_metrics.description: USC AMI bridges the gap between biomedical innovation and the creation of commercially successful medical products to improve and save lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biomedical inventors and teams should consult AMI for translation, commercialization, and product-development pathways tailored to medical technologies.
